Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The players and umpires return to the park.  Esha Oza and Theertha Satish are the openers for United Arab Emirates Women. It will be Renuka Singh to steam in with the ball for India Women. Let's go...
...THE RUN CHASE...

Right then, the target for United Arab Emirates Women is a stiff one and they will come up against some world class bowlers as well. United Arab Emirates Women a good start in the Powerplay if they are to get anywhere close to the target and if they do so, this could be a cracking contest. Join us soon as the run chase is up next.

United Arab Emirates Women had their moments in the first innings but will feel that they have let it slip in the last few overs. Kavisha Egodage was the pick of the bowler with her early burst in the Powerplay where she picked up a couple of wickets. The frontline bowlers were certainly expensive and even when the fielding was good, the field placements could have been better. Skipper, Esha Oza also bowled a loose over in the middle phase which let the opposition batters get away with ease and they hardly had any answers with the ball barring a couple of bowlers who were a tad unlucky.

What a boundary-hitting extravaganza at the death from Richa Ghosh and she finishes unbeaten on 64 off just 29 balls taking India Women to their highest-ever T20I total. The intensity was always there from the Indian batters even when they lost wickets in a heap and managed to stitch together a couple of stands and get a big score on the board. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma were quick off the blocks with the latter hitting the ball to the fence with regularity. However, they had a bit of a slump in the Powerplay and we're 56/3 when Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues put on a steady stand. Jemimah fell but Kaur kept going and brought up a fifty as Richa Ghosh looked dangerous at the other end and went berserk in the final over, getting 20 runs off it in order to hand India the advantage at the halfway mark.

FOUR! What a finish! Richa Ghosh with five boundaries in a row to propel India Women to their first total of beyond 200 runs in a T20I game. Short of a length and at the stumps, Ghosh rocks back and powers the ball flat over mid on for a boundary. India Women finish with 201/5 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of United Arab Emirates Women. It will be the usual opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma who will open the innings for India Women. Samaira Dharnidharka has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
As the wait for the first ball continues, visuals earlier showed Tanuja Kanwar receiving her maiden cap for the national side. A proud moment for her.

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is pitch side. She says that it's a 59-meter boundary all around the ground. Adds that the wind will play a huge factor on one side. Shares that they are at Pitch 4 and it has a bit more grass and looks hard. Ends by adding that the spinners will have a huge role to play.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women says that they wanted to bat first so they are happy with it. Adds that they will go with the flow and look to set a challenging total. Mentions that they will see how they start and tinker with the batting order accordingly. Informs that Shreyanka Patil is not playing and Tanuja Kanwar comes in place of her.

Esha Oza, the skipper of United Arab Emirates Women, says that it’s a fresh wicket and they will try to restrict India to as low  a total as possible. Shares that they need to learn from their game against Nepal and do the basics right. Ends by adding that they are going with the same side.

United Arab Emirates Women (Unchanged XI) - Esha Oza (C), Theertha Satish (WK), Rinitha Rajith, Samaira Dharnidharka, Kavisha Egodage, Khushi Sharma, Heena Hotchandani, Vaishnave Mahesh, Rithika Rajith, Lavanya Keny, Indhuja Nandakumar.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Dayalan Hemalatha, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Renuka Singh, Tanuja Kanwar (On debut) (In place of Shreyanka Patil).
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of United Arab Emirates Women and they have elected to BOWL first.

United Arab Emirates Women on the other hand suffered a huge loss against Nepal Women, a game they would have expected to be on the winning end of. However, they now face a stern test with games against India and Pakistan. Can UAE rise up to the challenge and inflict what would be an unprecedented defeat upon the reigning champs? Or will India make it two wins out of two? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Reigning champions, India Women asserted their claim as the favorites with a clinical win against arch rivals Pakistan Women in their opening encounter and will be looking to cruise to victory yet again and get one foot in the knockout phase of the competition.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one and all. We are in Dambulla for Match 5 of the Women's Asia Cup 2024 where India Women will go up against United Arab Emirates Women in a Group A clash. This will be the second game for both sides with the two sides starting their campaign in contrasting fashion.
... MATCH DAY ...

Women's T20 Asia Cup has erupted into action! Teams from across the Asian continent are locked in a fierce battle, each team hungry to claim the glittering trophy and etch their name in Asian cricket history. Match number 5 features the probable favorites India Women taking on the women of the United Arab Emirates in Group A. The Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, Dambulla continues to serve as the exclusive venue for this competition. India Women opened their Asia Cup campaign with a masterclass performance against their neighbors, Pakistan Women. They didn't just edge past their opponents, they outplayed them comprehensively. Initiating any tournament campaign with a win is like scoring a first-ball boundary - it sets the tone for what's to come. And boy, did India Women make a statement! In the most anticipated clash of the Asia Cup, India's bowling attack turned up the heat, leaving Pakistan's batters feeling the pressure. It was a masterclass in spin and seam, with the bowlers hitting their lengths and keeping the opposition guessing. When it was time to chase, India's batting lineup showed they were in no mood for a close contest. The in-form opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma carried their golden touch from the South Africa series into this crucial match. The middle order hasn't really been tested yet, but they must be ready to step up and make a difference when needed. Coming into this clash, it presents a golden opportunity for the Indian team to not only sharpen their skills further but also to cement their position in the semifinals. After a tough loss to Nepal Women, the UAE squad is eager to notch their first win in the tournament. However, they've got a big challenge ahead against a strong Indian side. The UAE's top order batters know they need to step up and set a solid foundation. The middle order will rely heavily on in-form players like Kavisha Egodage and Khushi Sharma to deliver strong finishes and cover any lapses. Overall, for the UAE women to pose a serious challenge, they'll need to elevate their game across the board, as a defeat here will mathematically put an end to their journey in this competition. Sure, the Indian side is far more experienced than them but T20 cricket has always thrown some unimaginable surprises, which, surely cannot be overlooked here. Will the UAE women led by Esha Oza induce a good challenge, or will Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. continue on their triumph? Who do you think will come out as a better side?
